extracted.intended_audience: scholars and researchers in comparative psychology and anthropology (members of learned societies)
extracted.subtask_description: Outline for organising and carrying out comparative psychology research on human types: proposes a three-division map (general mental evolution; sex-differences; special mental traits) and lists specific mental traits and questions to investigate under each heading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary general survey / mapping of subject
rubrics_metrics.description: That making a general survey is useful as a preliminary to deliberate study, either of a whole or of any part; Vagueness of thought accompanies wandering about in a region without known bounds or landmarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before detailed inquiries, map out the whole subject so parts are conceived in relation to the whole. A good survey prevents untrue conceptions and facilitates methodic inquiry and division of labour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic division and order of increasing speciality
rubrics_metrics.description: To map out the Comparative Psychology of Man must also conduce to the more methodic carrying on of inquiries. Division of labour will facilitate progress; and that there may be division of labour, the work itself must be systematically divided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate the subject into three main divisions and arrange them in the order of increasing speciality so that division of labour and coordinated inquiry are possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division I — Degrees of mental evolution (general mental evolution)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first division will treat of the degrees of mental evolution of different human types, generally considered: taking account of both the mass of mental manifestation and the complexity of mental manifestation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include relations of these characters to physical characters (bodily mass and structure, cerebral mass and structure); inquire into time taken to complete mental evolution, duration of adult mental power, and general traits such as persistence of emotions and intellectual processes; study connexion between general mental type and general social type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division II — Relative mental natures of the sexes
rubrics_metrics.description: In the second division place inquiries concerning the relative mental natures of the sexes in each race: questions about differences of mental mass and complexity between males and females, their variation, and causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask whether differences are common to all races, whether they vary in degree or kind, whether they change with time, and what relations they bear to habits of life, domestic arrangements, and social arrangements; include sentiments of the sexes towards one another and towards offspring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division III — Special mental traits distinguishing types
rubrics_metrics.description: The third division reserves the more special mental traits distinguishing different types of men: differences from proportion among common faculties or presence/absence of faculties in some races.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each discovered difference, study connections with stage of mental evolution and with habits of life and social development, treating causes and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mental mass
rubrics_metrics.description: Daily experiences show us that human beings differ in volume of mental manifestation. Some produce little impression while others, even uttering commonplaces, affect listeners disproportionately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate relations between mental mass and (a) bodily mass, (b) brain mass, (c) physiological state (circulation, blood richness) as determined by mode of life and nutrition, and (d) social state (nomadic/settled, predatory/industrial). Consider how differences in emotional energy contribute to social dominance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mental complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: How races differ with respect to more or less involved structures of their minds — analogous to differences between juvenile and adult minds (absorption in facts vs. recognition of generalities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare kinds and amounts of complexity between groups. Ask (a) relation between mental complexity and mental mass (do they vary together?), and (b) relation to social complexity (do mental and social complexity act and react on each other?).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate of mental development
rubrics_metrics.description: In conformity with the biological law that the higher the organisms the longer they take to evolve, inferior human races may complete mental evolution sooner than superior races; travellers note precocity and early arrest among savage and semi-civilized peoples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask whether the contrast holds consistently across groups; secondary inquiries include (a) whether rate differences show unequally in sexes, (b) relation between arrest period and puberty, (c) whether rapid evolution implies early mental decay, and (d) whether the entire mental cycle (birth to death) spans a shorter interval in lower types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative plasticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there relation between degree of mental modifiability remaining in adult life and the character of mental evolution in respect of mass, complexity, and rapidity? Lowly organized creatures show more automatic, less modifiable behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate whether more highly developed minds are more plastic; relate plasticity to precocity, early completion of development, and to social state (rigidity of custom vs. modifiability). Use traveller accounts and historical evidence to compare modifiability across societies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variability (short-term inconstancy vs long-term stability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between minute-to-minute inconstancy of manifestations and average manifestations extending over long periods — apparent contradiction reconciled when short-term changeability coexists with long-term unchangeableness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study how high short-term variability (e.g., infant alternating smiles/tears) can coexist with long-term average stability; investigate implications for characterising minds and for comparative classification.
